questions.title: The Khumalo Family Budget — Income, Percentages, Ratio and Inflation

subQuestions.questionText: The Khumalo family: Mr Khumalo works 20 days per month at a daily rate of R1 650, and earns R12 500 per month renting out a second property. Mrs Khumalo earns a net monthly income of R20 000. Calculate the Khumalo family's net collective income.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mr Khumalo salary = 20 × R1 650 = R33 000
Collective income = R33 000 + R12 500 + R20 000 = R65 500

Mark 1: 20 × R1 650
Mark 2: adding R12 500 and R20 000
Mark 3: answer R65 500

subQuestions.questionText: The Khumalo's bond repayment is R12 300. Mr Khumalo's monthly salary is 20 × R1 650 = R33 000. Determine what percentage of Mr Khumalo's monthly salary is used to repay their bond.
subQuestions.memoText:
Percentage = R12 300 ÷ R33 000 × 100
= 37,27%

Mark 1: R12 300 as the numerator
Mark 2: ÷ R33 000
Mark 3: × 100 → 37,27%

subQuestions.questionText: The Grade 1 to 7 monthly school fee is R2 300 per child. The Grade R monthly school fee is 4/5 of the Grade 1 to 7 school fee. One child is in Grade R and the other in Grade 2. Calculate the total monthly school fee for both children.
subQuestions.memoText:
Grade R fee = 4/5 × R2 300 = R1 840
Total = R2 300 + R1 840 = R4 140
(OR R2 300 + 80% × R2 300 = R4 140)

Mark 1: 4/5 (or 80%) of R2 300
Mark 2: adding the two fees
Mark 3: answer R4 140

subQuestions.questionText: Both children travel to and from school by scholar transport. Mr Khumalo pays R15,00 per one-way (single) trip per child. There are 20 school days in a month. Calculate the amount Mr Khumalo pays for transport for both children.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cost = R15 × 2 trips (there and back) × 2 children × 20 days
= R1 200

Mark 1: R15 × 2 (return journey)
Mark 2: × 2 children × 20 days
Mark 3: answer R1 200

subQuestions.questionText: The Khumalos budget 5% of Mrs Khumalo's net monthly income of R20 000 for municipal expenses. Calculate this amount.
subQuestions.memoText:
Municipal budget = 0,05 × R20 000 = R1 000

Mark 1: 5% of R20 000
Mark 2: answer R1 000

subQuestions.questionText: Two years ago the family spent an average of R6 500 per month on groceries. The average rate of inflation is 5,46%. The table already shows: cost two years ago R6 500, percentage increase amount R354,90, inflated amount a year ago R6 854,90. Determine the percentage increase amount for last year and the current amount per month budgeted for groceries.
subQuestions.memoText:
Percentage increase amount (last year) = 0,0546 × R6 854,90 = R374,28
Current amount = R6 854,90 + R374,28 = R7 229,18
(OR R6 854,90 × 105,46% = R7 229,18)

Mark 1: 0,0546 × R6 854,90
Mark 2: R374,28
Mark 3: adding to R6 854,90
Mark 4: current amount R7 229,18

subQuestions.questionText: The Khumalo family budgets money for entertainment and money saved for emergencies in a ratio of 2 : 5. If the family saves R3 000 for emergencies per month, how much do they spend on entertainment?
subQuestions.memoText:
Entertainment = R3 000 ÷ 5 × 2 = R1 200
(OR R3 000 ÷ 2,5 = R1 200)

Mark 1: R3 000 ÷ 5 (one part)
Mark 2: × 2
Mark 3: answer R1 200

subQuestions.questionText: A table of South African fuel prices per litre for 2024 includes: January R22,17; February R22,92; March R24,13; April R24,78; May R25,15; June R23,91; July R22,86. Calculate the difference between January and May 2024's fuel price per litre.
subQuestions.memoText:
Difference = R25,15 − R22,17 = R2,98

Mark 1: identifying January (R22,17)
Mark 2: identifying May (R25,15)
Mark 3: subtraction → R2,98

subQuestions.questionText: Which measure of central tendency does the answer to Question 1.8.1 (R2,98) represent?
subQuestions.memoText:
Range.

(Note: R2,98 is the difference between the maximum and minimum values, i.e. the range — which is actually a measure of spread/dispersion rather than central tendency.)

[Award 2 marks for 'range']

subQuestions.questionText: Is the data for the fuel price per litre continuous or discrete?
subQuestions.memoText:
Continuous (a fuel price is a measured monetary value that can take any value within a range).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The dollar-to-rand exchange rates in the table are: January 18,7254; February 18,9030; March 18,8263; April 18,6707; May 18,6120; June 18,9046; July 18,4146. During which month was the exchange rate the second highest?
subQuestions.memoText:
February (R18,9030) — the highest is June (R18,9046), so February is the second highest.

[Award 2 marks]

questions.title: Joseph's Coffee Kiosk — Graphs, Averages and a Cost/Income Table

subQuestions.questionText: Joseph finds a graph showing the predicted increase in the value of the global coffee market, using a picture/icon of a coffee cup repeated to represent the value for each year. What type of graph is this?
subQuestions.memoText:
A pictograph (also accept: bar graph).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State the value of the global coffee market in 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
$465,9 billion (i.e. $465 900 000 000)

[Award 2 marks for reading the 2020 value from the graph]

subQuestions.questionText: The predicted value of the global coffee market in 2026 is $668,4 billion. Determine the predicted increase amount in the value of the global coffee market from 2020 ($465,9 billion) to 2026.
subQuestions.memoText:
Increase = $668,4 billion − $465,9 billion = $202,5 billion ($202 500 000 000)

Mark 1: subtraction
Mark 2: answer $202,5 billion

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the predicted percentage increase in the value of the global coffee market between 2020 ($465,9 billion) and 2026 ($668,4 billion). Use: Predicted percentage increase = (difference in predicted price ÷ original price) × 100%.

Joseph finds a bar graph of the highest coffee consumption (in kg) per person per country. The graph has a set of dots (an ellipsis) marked with the letter A between some of the bars. Explain the use of the dots in the bar graph illustrated by the letter A.
subQuestions.memoText:
The dots show that part of the graph has been left out — the values/positions 11 to 13 (the countries ranked 11th to 13th) have been omitted so that only the relevant bars are shown.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The top 10 highest coffee consumers have an average consumption of 6,12 kg per person. The other 9 countries (excluding Switzerland) have a combined consumption of 56,4 kg. Show that the average amount of coffee consumed in Switzerland is 4,8 kg per person.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total for the top 10 = 6,12 × 10 = 61,2 kg
Switzerland = 61,2 − 56,4 = 4,8 kg per person ✓

Mark 1: 6,12 × 10 = 61,2
Mark 2: subtracting 56,4
Mark 3: answer 4,8 kg per person

subQuestions.questionText: Give the median amount of coffee consumed by the top 10 highest coffee consumers, given that the 5th and 6th values in the ordered data are 5,5 kg and 5,3 kg.
subQuestions.memoText:
Median = (5,5 + 5,3) ÷ 2 = 5,4 kg per person

Mark 1: adding the two middle values
Mark 2: ÷ 2 → 5,4 kg

subQuestions.questionText: The costs of running Joseph's coffee kiosk per day are: fixed costs of R500 rental per day, and variable costs of R5,50 per cup of coffee. Give an equation Joseph can use to calculate the cost (R) per day in terms of the number of cups (n) of coffee sold per day.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cost (R) = 500 + 5,5n

Mark 1: format (Cost = …)
Mark 2: fixed cost 500
Mark 3: the term 5,5n

subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows Joseph's cost per day and income per day for different numbers of cups of coffee. Some values are omitted.

Number of cups (n): 0 | 1 | 10 | 20 | C | 100
Cost per day (R): A | 505,50 | 555,00 | 610,00 | 665,00 | D
Income per day (R): 0 | B | 200,00 | 400,00 | 600,00 | 2 000,00

Calculate the values of A, B, C and D.
subQuestions.memoText:
A = cost at 0 cups = 500 + 5,5(0) = R500
Income per cup = R200 ÷ 10 = R20, so B = income at 1 cup = R20
Cost of R665,00: 500 + 5,5C = 665 → 5,5C = 165 → C = 30 cups
D = cost at 100 cups = 500 + 5,5(100) = R1 050

Mark 1–2: A = R500
Mark 3–4: B = R20
Mark 5–6: C = 30 cups
Mark 7–8: D = R1 050

subQuestions.questionText: Use the values in the table from Question 2.3.2 to plot the cost and the income on the graph provided. Provide a suitable heading and label the axes. State the key features your graph must show.
subQuestions.memoText:
Suitable heading, e.g. "Cost and Income Comparison for Coffee Stall".
Vertical axis label: Cost and Income (Rand). Horizontal axis label: Number of cups of coffee.
A key distinguishing the Cost line from the Income line.
Income line: straight line through (0; 0) and (100; 2 000).
Cost line: straight line through (0; 500) and (100; 1 050).
Dotted projection lines where used.
The lines cross at about n = 34 cups (the break-even point).

Mark 1: suitable heading
Mark 2: axis labels
Mark 3: key
Mark 4: Income point (0; 0)
Mark 5: Income point (100; 2 000)
Mark 6: Cost point (0; 500)
Mark 7: Cost point (100; 1 050)
Mark 8: dotted lines / accurate straight lines

questions.title: Salaries: South Africa vs USA — Income Tax, Exchange Rates and Trends

subQuestions.questionText: Using the 2023/2024 tax table, calculate how much tax a South African below age 65, earning an average gross salary of R303 648 per year, will pay per month if the person pays R3 795,60 towards pension every month. Tax table: R0 – R237 100: 18% of taxable income; R237 101 – R370 500: R42 678 + 26% of taxable income above R237 100. Primary rebate (below 65): R17 235.
subQuestions.memoText:
Annual pension = R3 795,60 × 12 = R45 547,20
Taxable income = R303 648 − R45 547,20 = R258 100,80
Bracket: R237 101 – R370 500
Tax = R42 678 + 0,26 × (R258 100,80 − R237 100)
= R42 678 + 0,26 × R21 000,80
= R42 678 + R5 460,21
= R48 138,21
Less primary rebate: R48 138,21 − R17 235 = R30 903,21 per year
Monthly tax = R30 903,21 ÷ 12 = R2 575,27 per month

Mark 1: R3 795,60 × 12
Mark 2: gross − annual pension
Mark 3: identifying the tax bracket
Mark 4: R258 100,80 − R237 100
Mark 5: 42 678 + 26% of the excess
Mark 6: subtracting the primary rebate only
Mark 7: ÷ 12 → R2 575,27

subQuestions.questionText: The average salary in the USA is $1 100 per week. The average South African gross salary is R303 648 per year. Compare the average annual salaries of South Africa and the USA to determine which country has the highest average salary, if $1 = R18,83.
subQuestions.memoText:
USA annual = $1 100 × 52 weeks = $57 200 per year
In rand: $57 200 × R18,83 = R1 077 076 per year
SA annual = R303 648 per year
R1 077 076 > R303 648
Therefore the USA has the highest average salary.

Mark 1: $1 100 × 52
Mark 2: $57 200
Mark 3: converting to rand (× 18,83)
Mark 4: R1 077 076
Mark 5: conclusion — USA has the higher average salary

subQuestions.questionText: A graph shows the change in the average annual income in South Africa from 1946 to 2016. The red line for 2016 shows an average annual income of R108 313. What was the average national monthly income (red line) in 2016?
subQuestions.memoText:
Monthly income = R108 313 ÷ 12 = R9 026,08

Mark 1: dividing the annual value by 12
Mark 2: answer R9 026,08

subQuestions.questionText: According to the graph, in which year was the gross domestic product the highest?
subQuestions.memoText:
1980

[Award 2 marks for reading the graph correctly]

subQuestions.questionText: According to the graph, what was the average annual income in 1990?
subQuestions.memoText:
R100 000

[Award 2 marks for reading the graph correctly]

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the trend in the national income from 1946 to 1980.
subQuestions.memoText:
After an initial dip, the national income rises to a maximum around 1974. This is followed by a sudden, sharp decrease, before the income quickly rises again.

[Award marks for: initial dip; rise to a peak (~1974); sharp decrease then recovery]

subQuestions.questionText: In 2023 the minimum wage in South Africa was R25,42 per hour. From 1 March 2024 the Department of Labour increased the minimum wage by 8,497%. Determine how much the minimum wage for a month will be after the 2024 increase if a worker works 40 hours per week.
subQuestions.memoText:
New hourly rate = R25,42 + 0,08497 × R25,42 = R25,42 × 1,08497 = R27,58 per hour
Monthly wage = R27,58 × 40 hours × 4 weeks = R4 412,80
(OR R25,42 × 40 × 4 = R4 067,20; R4 067,20 × 1,08497 = R4 412,79)

Mark 1: 8,497% of R25,42
Mark 2: new rate R27,58
Mark 3: × 40 hours
Mark 4: × 4 weeks
Mark 5: answer R4 412,80

subQuestions.questionText: A table shows the average annual net salary in South Africa by city, in descending order: East London R296 429; Johannesburg R295 000; Cape Town A; Pretoria R252 000; Durban R226 000; Port Elizabeth R212 000; Pietermaritzburg R203 000; Vereeniging R194 000; Kimberley B; Bloemfontein C. Also: the range is R109 429; the upper quartile is R269 000; the mode is R203 000. Determine the missing values A, B and C.
subQuestions.memoText:
A = upper quartile = R269 000 (Cape Town is the middle value of the top 5 salaries)
B = mode = R203 000 (Kimberley must repeat R203 000 for it to be the mode)
C = minimum = maximum − range = R296 429 − R109 429 = R187 000 (Bloemfontein)

Mark 1: A = R269 000
Mark 2: B = R203 000
Mark 3: C = R187 000

questions.title: Boeing 747 Flight Costs — Exchange Rates, Cost Breakdown and Box Plots

subQuestions.questionText: A Boeing 747 flight from Johannesburg to Cape Town could cost up to R1 914 404,00, which equals $101 463,41. Determine the rand-to-dollar exchange rate at the time, in the form $1 = ______, to four decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
$1 = R1 914 404,00 ÷ $101 463,41
= R18,8679

Mark 1: dividing rand by dollars
Mark 2: exchange rate value
Mark 3: rounding to 4 decimal places → $1 = R18,8679

subQuestions.questionText: The minimum flight cost is R1 148 642,40 and the flight carries 400 passengers. Determine, in rands, the cost per passenger.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cost per passenger = R1 148 642,40 ÷ 400 = R2 871,61

Mark 1: identifying the minimum cost
Mark 2: dividing by 400
Mark 3: answer R2 871,61

subQuestions.questionText: Each of the 400 passengers has an average mass of 80 kg. Using the minimum flight cost of R1 148 642,40, find the average cost, in rands, per kilogram of passenger mass.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total passenger mass = 400 × 80 = 32 000 kg
Cost per kg = R1 148 642,40 ÷ 32 000 = R35,90 per kg
(OR R2 871,61 ÷ 80 = R35,90 per kg)

Mark 1: 400 × 80
Mark 2: 32 000 kg
Mark 3: dividing the minimum cost by 32 000
Mark 4: answer R35,90 per kg

subQuestions.questionText: A cost-breakdown graph shows Flight Attendants = 1% of the flight cost. The cost of a two-hour flight from Johannesburg to Cape Town is R1 148 642,40. The ratio of air hostesses to passengers is 1 : 50 and there are 400 passengers. Show that an air hostess will earn R717,90 per hour on this flight.
subQuestions.memoText:
Number of air hostesses = 400 ÷ 50 = 8
Flight Attendants cost = 1% × R1 148 642,40 = R11 486,42
Per hostess (2-hour flight) = R11 486,42 ÷ 8 = R1 435,80
Per hour = R1 435,80 ÷ 2 = R717,90 per hour ✓

Mark 1: 400 ÷ 50 = 8 hostesses
Mark 2: 1% of R1 148 642,40
Mark 3: R11 486
Mark 4: ÷ 8
Mark 5: ÷ 2 → R717,90 per hour

subQuestions.questionText: On the cost-breakdown pie graph, Landing Fees make up 9% of the cost. Calculate the size (in degrees) of the sector allocated to Landing Fees.

A box-and-whisker plot summarises the mass of luggage (in kg) per passenger on a Johannesburg–Cape Town flight. The median is 45 kg, which is also the airline's recommended mass limit. State the percentage of passengers whose luggage was below the recommended mass limit.
subQuestions.memoText:
50% (the recommended limit of 45 kg is the median, so half of the passengers are below it).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: A quarter of the passengers had to pay a charge because their luggage was excessively overweight. On the box-and-whisker plot the upper quartile is 58 kg. What is the lowest luggage mass within this group?
subQuestions.memoText:
58 kg (the upper quartile — the top 25% of the data lies at or above it).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The lower quartile of the luggage data is 36 kg and the upper quartile is 58 kg. Determine the interquartile range of the data spread.
subQuestions.memoText:
IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 58 − 36 = 22 kg

Mark 1: Q3 − Q1
Mark 2: answer 22 kg

subQuestions.questionText: The + sign on the box-and-whisker plot indicates an outlier. Explain what you understand by the term 'outlier'.
subQuestions.memoText:
An outlier is a value in a data set that is very different from (much larger or much smaller than) all the other values in the data set.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The data is skewed to the (right / left). Highlight or underline the correct answer within the bracket.
subQuestions.memoText:
right (skewed to the right — the longer tail / whisker is on the higher-value side).

[Award 2 marks]

questions.title: Athletic Footwear — Compound Growth, VAT, Probability and Misleading Graphs

subQuestions.questionText: In 2024 the revenue in the athletic footwear segment of South Africa is expected to reach $150,80 million. Write out $150,80 million in numbers, without the comma and without the word 'million'.
subQuestions.memoText:
$150 800 000

Mark 1: correct digits
Mark 2: correct place value (150 800 000)

subQuestions.questionText: The athletic footwear market has an annual growth rate of 4,35% (2024–2028). 801 223 pairs of shoes will be sold by the end of 2024, and this is predicted to reach 0,95 million pairs by the end of 2028. Complete the table (values A, B, C, D — the missing starting numbers and percentage-increase amounts) to show that the statement is true.
The VAYA Victory Lap 1 athletic footwear costs R1 299,99 (inclusive of 15% VAT). With calculations, determine the VAT amount payable to SARS.
subQuestions.memoText:
Amount excluding VAT = R1 299,99 ÷ 1,15 = R1 130,43
VAT = R1 299,99 − R1 130,43 = R169,56
(OR R1 299,99 × 15/115 = R169,56)

Mark 1: dividing by 1,15 (or × 15/115)
Mark 2: subtracting the VAT-exclusive amount
Mark 3: answer R169,56

subQuestions.questionText: What does the acronym SARS stand for?
subQuestions.memoText:
South African Revenue Service

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 5.3.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: VAYA sells two shoe types (Victory Lap 1, Triumph) in a range of colours, shown on a tree diagram. P(Victory Lap 1) = 1/2 and there are 5 colour options for it (each equally likely). Write down the probability that a customer would select a Beige Victory Lap 1 shoe, labelled A on the tree diagram.
subQuestions.memoText:
P(A) = 1/2 × 1/5 = 1/10

Mark 1: product of the two branch probabilities
Mark 2: answer 1/10

subQuestions.label: 5.3.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: P(Triumph) = 1/2 and there are 4 equally likely colour options for the Triumph. Calculate the probability that a customer will, at random, select a Beige Triumph shoe, labelled B.
subQuestions.memoText:
P(B) = 1/2 × 1/4 = 1/8

Mark 1: product of the two branch probabilities
Mark 2: answer 1/8

subQuestions.label: 5.3.3 (c)
subQuestions.questionText: Write the probability of selecting a Beige Victory Lap 1 shoe (1/10) as a decimal and as a percentage.
subQuestions.memoText:
Decimal: 0,1
Percentage: 10%

Mark 1: decimal 0,1
Mark 2: percentage 10%

subQuestions.questionText: The VAYA online store sells 50 pairs of athletic footwear in a week. The prices of the footwear are: R950; R1 100; R1 200; R1 299,99; and R1 400. Show that the mean (average) income earned in a month is R237 999,60.
What is the range of prices of the footwear? (Prices: R950; R1 100; R1 200; R1 299,99; R1 400.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Range = R1 400 − R950 = R450

Mark 1: max − min
Mark 2: answer R450

subQuestions.questionText: Why is it more important to know the modal shoe size sold than the average shoe size sold?
subQuestions.memoText:
The modal (most frequently sold) size tells the shop which size sells the most, so they can order enough stock of it. An average shoe size could work out to a value that no customer actually wears (e.g. a size that is not made), so it is not useful for planning stock.

[Award 2 marks for a valid reason]

subQuestions.questionText: A magazine screenshot shows a graph of readers' preferences for the height of their high-heel shoes, from a poll. Give a reason why the graph in the image can be considered misleading to readers.
subQuestions.memoText:
The bars of the graph represent the heel height, not the percentage of readers who preferred that height, so the bars actually get shorter as the percentage gets larger. A reader glancing at it would think the tallest bar is the most popular choice, when the opposite is true.

[Award 2 marks for a valid reason]
